newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia T-bill premion to depend on foreign demand.
newsitem.headline: Russia T-bill premion to depend on foreign demand.

text.p: Russian investors at Wednesday's auction of 364-day Treasury bills will bid aggressively, aiming for a yield premium over current market rates, but whether they succeed will depend on foreign demand, dealers said on Tuesday.
TOMORROW
Finance Ministry sells:
*7.50 trln rbls 364-day T-bills (series 23006)
*4.00 trln rbls 161-day T-bills (series 22082)
Finance Ministry repays/pays:
*7.25 trln rbls maturing 140-day T-bills (series 22063)
*468.64 bln rbls in interest payment on series 24006 OFZ interest-bearing bond
TODAY
*Average yield fell to 28.6 pct from 29.2 pct
*Turnover rose to 5.28 trln rbls from 2.93 trln rbls
*Series 22079 bills closed to yield 29.01 pct
*Series 23005 bills closed to yield 30.52 pct
*Central Bank did not intervene
Dealers forecast the average yield on series 23006 bills, maturing on May 6, 1998, would be in the 30.61-31.58 percent.
The series 23005 bills, maturing on April 22, 1998, closed at 77.31 to yield 30.52 percent.
The average yield on series 22082 bills, maturing on October 15, 1997, would be in the 28.91-30.71 percent.
The series 22079 bills, maturing on October 22, 1997, closed at 88.16 to yield 29.01 percent.

"I cannot see a lively interest to the auctions," said MFK dealer Andrei Koshchi. "I cannot see an inflow of fresh funds from non-residents from the amount of funds in the system -- the rise is due to unwillingness to sell and portfolio restructuring."
Dealers said dollar sales on the foreign exchange market as happened today did not necessarily herald a successful auction, as roubles from the sales could be used for other purposes.
"It happened more than once -- big volumes of hard currency were sold on the interbank market, but we did not see the money," a dealer said. "It will not necessarily go to the exchange."
But Sergei Koshelenko, head of forex at CS First Boston, forecast a good auction on Wednesday.

"The hard currency market is stable with rouble depreciation slowing down, and so is the T-bill market. That's why there will be no premium. I think the yields will be in line with the secondary market," he said.
Andrei Vetrov, an analyst at Moscow Narodny Bank, Moscow forecast a strong demand and a premium due to aggressive bids.

"It is not the volume of funds which is important, but investors' mood. The volume of offer and repayment is quite big and I think there will be enough room for both competitive and non-competitive bids," he said.
--Anna Smirnova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
